title: 1. ଲେଖକ ପରିଚୟ (Writer Introduction)
content: William Wordsworth (1770-1850) ଇଂରାଜୀ ସାହିତ୍ୟର ଜଣେ ମହାନ ପ୍ରକୃତିକ କବି ଅଟନ୍ତି। ସେ ଇଂଲଣ୍ଡରେ ଜନ୍ମଗ୍ରହଣ କରିଥିଲେ। ସେ ପ୍ରକୃତିକୁ ମଣିଷର ମହାନ ଶିକ୍ଷକ ଭାବରେ ବିବେଚନା କରନ୍ତି ଏବଂ ତାଙ୍କ କବିତାଗୁଡ଼ିକ ପ୍ରକୃତି ସହିତ ଏକ ନିବିଡ଼ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ସ୍ଥାପନ କରେ।

title: 2. ଲେଖକଙ୍କ ସାହିତ୍ୟିକ ପୃଷ୍ଠଭୂମି (Literary Background)
content: William Wordsworth 19ତମ ଶତାବ୍ଦୀର Romantic Movement ର ଅନ୍ୟତମ ପ୍ରତିଷ୍ଠାତା ଥିଲେ। ସେ ସରଳ ଗ୍ରାମାଞ୍ଚଳର ଜୀବନ ଏବଂ ପ୍ରକୃତିର ସୌନ୍ଦର୍ଯ୍ୟକୁ ନିଜ କବିତାରେ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଭାବରେ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରିଛନ୍ତି। ତାଙ୍କର ପ୍ରସିଦ୍ଧ ରଚନାଗୁଡ଼ିକ ମଧ୍ୟରେ Daffodils ଏବଂ The Solitary Reaper ଅନ୍ତର୍ଭୁକ୍ତ।

title: 3. ଲେଖକଙ୍କ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣ / ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ (Writer's View / Purpose)
content: ଏହି କବିତାର ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ କବି ଦର୍ଶାଇବାକୁ ଚାହାଁନ୍ତି ଯେ ପିଲାମାନେ ଦୁନିଆକୁ ଏକ ସରଳ ଏବଂ ନିର୍ମଳ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣରୁ ଦେଖନ୍ତି। ବୟସ୍କମାନଙ୍କ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ଧାରଣା ଏବଂ ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କର ନିରୀହ ହୃଦୟର ଅନନ୍ତ ଭାବନା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଥକ୍ୟକୁ ଏଠାରେ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଭାବରେ ଉପସ୍ଥାପନ କରାଯାଇଛି।

title: 4. ଅଧ୍ୟାୟ ପରିଚୟ (Chapter Introduction)
content: We are Seven କବିତାଟି William Wordsworth ଙ୍କ ଦ୍ୱାରା ଲିଖିତ ଏକ ପ୍ରସିଦ୍ଧ କବିତା। ଏହା ଜଣେ ପରିପକ୍ୱ କବି ଏବଂ ଏକ ଆଠ ବର୍ଷର ଛୋଟ ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ ବାଳିକା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ହୋଇଥିବା କଥୋପକଥନ ଉପରେ ଆଧାରିତ। ବାଳିକାଟି ଜିଦ୍ ଧରି କହେ ଯେ ସେମାନେ ମୋଟ ସାତ ଜଣ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀ।

title: 5. ସରଳ କାହାଣୀ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା (Simple Story Narration)
content: କବି ଥରେ ଜଣେ ଆଠ ବର୍ଷର ଛୋଟ ଝିଅକୁ ଭେଟିଲେ ଏବଂ ତାଙ୍କ ପରିବାର ବିଷୟରେ ପଚାରିଲେ। ଝିଅଟି କହିଲା ଯେ ସେମାନେ ସାତ ଜଣ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀ ଅଛନ୍ତି। ସେମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ଦୁଇ ଜଣ Conway ରେ ରହନ୍ତି, ଦୁଇ ଜଣ ସମୁଦ୍ରକୁ ଯାଇଛନ୍ତି ଏବଂ ଦୁଇ ଜଣ କବରସ୍ଥାନରେ ଶୋଇଛନ୍ତି। କବି ବୁଝାଇଲେ ଯେ ମୃତମାନଙ୍କୁ ଛାଡ଼ିଲେ ସେମାନେ ମାତ୍ର ପାଞ୍ଚ ଜଣ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଝିଅଟି ଦୃଢ଼ ଭାବରେ କହିଲା ଯେ ସେମାନେ ସାତ ଜଣ ଅଛନ୍ତି।

title: 6. Stanza-wise Explanation - Stanza 1 to 3
content: ପ୍ରଥମ ସ୍ତବକରେ କବି ଜଣେ ସରଳ, ନିର୍ମଳ ଏବଂ ଜୀବନ୍ତ ଶିଶୁର କଥା କହିଛନ୍ତି ଯେ କି ଜୀବନର ପ୍ରତିଟି ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତକୁ ଉପଭୋଗ କରେ ଏବଂ ମୃତ୍ୟୁର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଅର୍ଥ ଜାଣେ ନାହିଁ।ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଓ ତୃତୀୟ ସ୍ତବକରେ କବି ଜଣେ ଆଠ ବର୍ଷର ସୁନ୍ଦର ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ ବାଳିକାକୁ ଭେଟିବା କାହାଣୀ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା କରିଛନ୍ତି, ଯାହାର କେଶରାଜି ଏବଂ ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ ସୌନ୍ଦର୍ଯ୍ୟ କବିଙ୍କ ମନକୁ ଆନନ୍ଦିତ କରିଥିଲା।

title: 7. Stanza-wise Explanation - Stanza 4 to 6
content: ଚତୁର୍ଥ ଓ ପଞ୍ଚମ ସ୍ତବକରେ କବି ଝିଅଟିକୁ ତାର ଭାଇଭଉଣୀଙ୍କ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ପଚାରିବାରୁ ସେ ଉତ୍ତର ଦିଏ ଯେ ସେମାନେ ସାତ ଜଣ ଅଛନ୍ତି। ଝିଅଟି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା କରେ ଯେ ଦୁଇ ଜଣ Conway ରେ ରହନ୍ତି, ଦୁଇ ଜଣ ସମୁଦ୍ରକୁ ଯାଇଛନ୍ତି ଏବଂ ଦୁଇ ଜଣ ଚର୍ଚ୍ଚର କବରସ୍ଥାନରେ ମାଆଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ଶୋଇଛନ୍ତି।

title: 8. Stanza-wise Explanation - Stanza 7 to 9
content: ଷଷ୍ଠ ଓ ସପ୍ତମ ସ୍ତବକରେ କବି ଯୁକ୍ତି କରନ୍ତି ଯେ ଯଦି ଦୁଇ ଜଣ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀ ମୃତ୍ୟୁବରଣ କରି କବରରେ ଅଛନ୍ତି, ତେବେ ବଞ୍ଚିଥିବା ପିଲାମାନେ ମାତ୍ର ପାଞ୍ଚ ଜଣ ହେବା କଥା। କିନ୍ତୁ ଛୋଟ ଝିଅଟି ପୁଣିଥରେ ଜିଦ୍ ଧରି କହେ ଯେ ସେମାନଙ୍କର ମୋଟ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ସାତ ଜଣ ଅଟେ।

title: 9. Stanza-wise Explanation - Stanza 10 to 12
content: ଏହି ସ୍ତବକଗୁଡ଼ିକରେ ଝିଅଟି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା କରେ ଯେ କିପରି ସେ ମୃତ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀଙ୍କ କବର ନିକଟରେ ବସି ମୋଜା ବୁଣେ, ରୁମାଲ ସିଏ ଏବଂ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଗୀତ ଗାଏ। ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟାସ୍ତ ପରେ ସେ ସେଠାରେ ନିଜର ରାତ୍ରୀଭୋଜନ ମଧ୍ୟ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରେ, ଯାହା ତାଙ୍କର ମୃତ ପ୍ରତି ଥିବା ଗଭୀର ଆତ୍ମୀୟତାକୁ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ।

title: 10. Stanza-wise Explanation - Stanza 13 to 16
content: ଶେଷ ସ୍ତବକଗୁଡ଼ିକରେ ବାଳିକାଟି ତାର ଭଉଣୀ ଜେନ୍ ଏବଂ ଭାଇ ଜନ୍ ର ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ଏବଂ ସେମାନଙ୍କ କବର ବିଷୟରେ କହେ। କବି ଯେତେ ବୁଝାଇବାକୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଯେ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ଆତ୍ମା ସ୍ୱର୍ଗରେ ଅଛି, ଝିଅଟି ନିଜର ଜିଦ୍ ରେ ଅଟଳ ରହି କହେ 'O Master! we are seven'।

title: 11. Difficult English Words with Odia Meaning
content: Cottage - ଛୋଟ ଘର ବା କୁଟିର। Rustic - ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ। Clustered - ଏକାଠି ଜମା ହୋଇଥିବା। Maid - ଝିଅ ବା ବାଳିକା। Dwell - ବାସ କରିବା ବା ରହିବା। Church-yard - ଚର୍ଚ୍ଚ ସଂଲଗ୍ନ କବରସ୍ଥାନ। Porringer - ସୂପ କିମ୍ବା ପରିଜ୍ ଖାଇବା ପାଇଁ ଏକ ଛୋଟ ପାତ୍ର। Moaning - କଷ୍ଟରେ କାନ୍ଦିବା ବା ଗ୍ରୀନ୍ କରିବା।

title: 12. New Vocabulary
content: Stockings - ଗୋଡ଼ ଏବଂ ପାଦ ପାଇଁ ତିଆରି ହୋଇଥିବା ପୋଷାକ। Kerchief - ମୁଣ୍ଡ କିମ୍ବା ବେକରେ ବନ୍ଧାଯାଉଥିବା ରୁମାଲ। Hem - କପଡ଼ାର କାନ୍ଥକୁ ମୋଡ଼ି ସିଲେଇ କରିବା। Spirits - ଆତ୍ମା ବା ପ୍ରାଣ। Wonder - ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟ ହେବା। Woodland - ଜଙ୍ଗଲପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଞ୍ଚଳ।

title: 13. Important Sentences with Explanation
content: 1. 'A simple Child, / That lightly draws its breath, / And feels its life in every limb, / What should it know of death?' - ଏହି ପଂକ୍ତିରେ କବି କହିଛନ୍ତି ଯେ ଜଣେ ସରଳ ଶିଶୁ ଜୀବନର ଆନନ୍ଦରେ ଭରା ଥାଏ ଏବଂ ମୃତ୍ୟୁର ଭୟଙ୍କର ଅର୍ଥ ବୁଝିବାକୁ ସକ୍ଷମ ହୋଇ ନଥାଏ।

title: 14. Characters
content: ଏହି କବିତାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟତଃ ଦୁଇଟି ଚରିତ୍ର ରହିଛନ୍ତି: 1. କବି (William Wordsworth) - ଯିଏ ଜଣେ ବୟସ୍କ ଏବଂ ଯୁକ୍ତିଯୁକ୍ତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଯିଏ ମୃତ୍ୟୁକୁ ଜୀବନର ଶେଷ ବୋଲି ଭାବନ୍ତି। 2. ଆଠ ବର୍ଷର ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ ବାଳିକା - ଯିଏ ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ସରଳ, ନିରୀହ ଏବଂ ମୃତ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀଙ୍କ ସହିତ ଆତ୍ମିକ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ବଜାୟ ରଖିଛି।

title: 15. Character Sketch of the Little Girl
content: ଆଠ ବର୍ଷର ଝିଅଟି ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ସୁନ୍ଦର, ସରଳ ଏବଂ ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ ପରିବେଶରେ ବଢ଼ିଥିବା ଏକ ବାଳିକା। ତାର ଆଖି ସୁନ୍ଦର ଏବଂ କେଶ କୁଣ୍ଡଳୀକୃତ। ସେ ମୃତ୍ୟୁକୁ ବିଚ୍ଛେଦ ଭାବରେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରେ ନାହିଁ, ବରଂ ତାର ମୃତ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀମାନେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାର ପରିବାରର ଅଂଶବିଶେଷ ବୋଲି ସେ ଦୃଢ଼ ଭାବରେ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ କରେ।

title: 16. Plot Summary
content: କବି ଜଣେ ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ ଝିଅକୁ ଭେଟି ତାଙ୍କ ପରିବାରର ସଦସ୍ୟ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ପଚାରିଲେ। ଝିଅଟି ସାତ ଜଣ ବୋଲି କହିବାରୁ କବି ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟ ହେଲେ, କାରଣ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ଦୁଇ ଜଣ ମୃତ୍ୟୁବରଣ କରିସାରିଥିଲେ। କବି ଯେତେ ବୁଝାଇଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଝିଅଟି ନିଜର ଦୃଢ଼ ବିଶ୍ୱାସରେ ଅଟଳ ରହିଲା ଯେ ସେମାନେ ସାତ ଜଣ ଅଛନ୍ତି।

title: 17. Sequence of Events
content: 1. କବି ଏକ ଆଠ ବର୍ଷର ଝିଅକୁ ଭେଟିବା। 2. କବି ଝିଅଟିକୁ ତାର ଭାଇଭଉଣୀଙ୍କ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ପଚାରିବା। 3. ଝିଅଟି ସେମାନେ ସାତ ଜଣ ବୋଲି କହିବା। 4. ଝିଅଟି ସେମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ଦୁଇ ଜଣ କବରସ୍ଥାନରେ ଥିବା କଥା କହିବା। 5. କବି ସେମାନେ ମାତ୍ର ପାଞ୍ଚ ଜଣ ବୋଲି ଯୁକ୍ତି କରିବା। 6. ଝିଅଟି ଜିଦ୍ ଧରି କହିବା ଯେ ସେମାନେ ସାତ ଜଣ ଅଛନ୍ତି।

title: 18. Central Idea
content: ଏହି କବିତାର କେନ୍ଦ୍ରୀୟ ଭାବ ହେଲା ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କର ନିରୀହତା ଏବଂ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ପ୍ରତି ସେମାନଙ୍କର ସରଳ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣ। ପିଲାମାନେ ପ୍ରିୟଜନଙ୍କ ମୃତ୍ୟୁକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ଠାରୁ ଦୂରେଇ ଯାଇଥିବାରୁ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ, ବରଂ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ସହିତ ଏକ ଆତ୍ମିକ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ସବୁବେଳେ ରଖିଥାଆନ୍ତି।

title: 19. Theme
content: କବିତାର ମୁଖ୍ୟ ଥିମ୍ ହେଲା ଶୈଶବର ନିରୀହତା, ପ୍ରକୃତିର ସୌନ୍ଦର୍ଯ୍ୟ ଏବଂ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ଓ ଜୀବନର ଅବିଚ୍ଛେଦ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପର୍କ। ବୟସ୍କମାନେ ମୃତ୍ୟୁକୁ ଶେଷ ବୋଲି ଭାବନ୍ତି, କିନ୍ତୁ ପିଲାମାନେ ମୃତ୍ୟୁକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ପ୍ରେମ ଓ ସ୍ମୃତିର ଏକ ବନ୍ଧନ ଭାବରେ ଦେଖନ୍ତି।

title: 20. Moral of the Story
content: ପ୍ରକୃତ ପ୍ରେମ ଏବଂ ପରିବାର ପ୍ରତି ଆକର୍ଷଣ କେବଳ ଶାରୀରିକ ଉପସ୍ଥିତିରେ ସୀମିତ ନୁହେଁ। ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କର ନିର୍ମଳ ହୃଦୟ ଏବଂ ନିରୀହ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ଆମ୍ଭକୁ ଶିକ୍ଷା ଦିଏ ଯେ ପ୍ରକୃତ ସମ୍ପୋକ କେବେ ମରେ ନାହିଁ।

title: 21. Writer's Message
content: କବି William Wordsworth ଏହି କବିତା ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ସନ୍ଦେଶ ଦେଇଛନ୍ତି ଯେ ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କର ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣ ବୟସ୍କମାନଙ୍କ ଅପେକ୍ଷା ଅଧିକ ସରଳ ଓ ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ ହୋଇଥାଏ। ସେମାନଙ୍କର ଭାବନା ଜଟିଳତାମୁକ୍ତ ଏବଂ ପ୍ରେମରେ ପରିପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ।

title: 22. Tone and Mood
content: ଏହି କବିତାର ଟୋନ୍ ଏବଂ ମୁଡ୍ ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଶାନ୍ତ, କାବ୍ଯିକ ଏବଂ ଆବେଗପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଟେ। କବିଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟଭାବ ଏବଂ ବାଳିକାଟିର ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଅଚଳ ବିଶ୍ୱାସର ଏକ ସୁନ୍ଦର ମିଶ୍ରଣ ଏଠାରେ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ମିଳେ।

title: 23. Literary Devices / Figures of Speech
content: ଏହି କବିତାରେ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଲିଟେରାରୀ ଡିଭାଇସ୍ ବ୍ୟବହୃତ ହୋଇଛି ଯେପରିକି Rhyme Scheme (ABAB), Imagery (ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ଏବଂ କବରସ୍ଥାନର ଚିତ୍ର), ଏବଂ Repetition ('We are seven' ବାକ୍ୟର ବାରମ୍ବାର ଆବୃତ୍ତି)।

title: 24. Grammar Points
content: ଏହି କବିତାରେ ବ୍ୟବହୃତ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ପ୍ରକାରର ସର୍ବନାମ (Pronouns) ଯେପରିକି I, she, we, they ଏବଂ କ୍ରିୟାପଦଗୁଡ଼ିକ (Verbs) କାହାଣୀର ପ୍ରବାହକୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର କରିଥାଏ। ଏଥିରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନବାଚକ ଏବଂ ବିବୃତିମୂଳକ ବାକ୍ୟର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ କରାଯାଇଛି।

title: 25. Important Exam Points
content: 1. କବିଙ୍କ ନାମ: William Wordsworth। 2. ବାଳିକାର ବୟସ: ଆଠ ବର୍ଷ। 3. ଝିଅଟିର ମୃତ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀଙ୍କ ନାମ: Jane ଏବଂ John। 4. କବିତାଟି କେଉଁଠାରୁ ନିଆଯାଇଛି: Goodrich Castle ନିକଟରେ କବିଙ୍କ ଅନୁଭୂତିରୁ। 5. କବିତାର ମୁଖ୍ୟ ଶ୍ଳୋକ: 'O Master! we are seven'।

title: 26. Complete Chapter Summary
content: We are Seven କବିତାଟି ଶୈଶବର ନିରୀହତା ଏବଂ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ବିଷୟରେ ଏକ ଗଭୀର ଚିନ୍ତାଧାରା ଉପରେ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟବସିତ। କବି ଜଣେ ଆଠ ବର୍ଷର ଝିଅକୁ ଭେଟି ତାଙ୍କ ପରିବାରର ସଦସ୍ୟ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ପଚାରିଲେ। ଝିଅଟି ଜିଦ୍ ଧରି କହିଲା ଯେ ସେମାନେ ସାତ ଜଣ, ଯଦିଓ ଦୁଇ ଜଣ ମୃତ୍ୟୁବରଣ କରି କବରରେ ଅଛନ୍ତି। କବିଙ୍କ ଯୁକ୍ତିକୁ ଅଗ୍ରାହ୍ୟ କରି ଝିଅଟି କହିଲା ଯେ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ସେମାନଙ୍କର ପରିବାର ବନ୍ଧନକୁ ଭାଙ୍ଗିପାରି ନାହିଁ।

title: 27. Chapter Conclusion
content: ଶେଷରେ, ଏହି କବିତା ଆମ୍ଭକୁ ଶିକ୍ଷା ଦିଏ ଯେ ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କର ହୃଦୟରେ ପ୍ରେମ ଏବଂ ସମ୍ପର୍କର ସୀମା କେବଳ ଶାରୀରିକ ଉପସ୍ଥିତିରେ ସୀମିତ ନଥାଏ। ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କର ନିରୀହ ମନରେ ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଛିନ୍ନ କରିପାରେ ନାହିଁ, ଯାହା ଏହି କବିତାର ସବୁଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ ସୌନ୍ଦର୍ଯ୍ୟ ଅଟେ।

title: 28. 10 Very Short Questions with Answers
content:
1. Who is the author of the poem 'We are Seven'? Ans: William Wordsworth. 
2. How old was the little cottage girl? Ans: Eight years old. 
3. Where did the poet meet the little girl? Ans: Near a cottage/wild forest in Wales. 
4. How many brothers and sisters did the girl say they were in all? Ans: Seven in all. 
5. Where did two of her brothers live? Ans: At Conway. 
6. Where had two of her brothers gone? Ans: To sea. 
7. Where were her sister and brother buried? Ans: In the church-yard. 
8. What was the name of her sister who died first? Ans: Jane. 
9. What was the name of her brother who died after Jane? Ans: John. 
10. What is the final statement of the little girl in the poem? Ans: 'O Master! we are seven'.

title: 29. 10 Short Questions with Answers
content:
1. What notable features of a simple child does the poet describe in the first stanza? Ans: The poet describes that a simple child lightly draws its breath and feels its life in every limb without knowing the true meaning of death. 
2. What was the appearance of the little girl? Ans: Her hair was thick with many curls clustered round her head, she had a rustic, woodland air, and was wildly clad with very fair eyes. 
3. Why did the girl look 'wondering' at the poet? Ans: The girl looked wondering because to her simple mind, her dead siblings were still a part of the family, and she could not understand why the poet kept counting them as five. 
4. What did the little girl do near the graves of her siblings? Ans: She often knitted her stockings, hemmed her kerchiefs, sat on the ground, sang a song, and ate her supper there. 
5. How did sister Jane suffer before her death? Ans: Sister Jane lay moaning in bed in pain until God released her and she went away. 
6. In what season did her brother John die? Ans: Her brother John died when the ground was white with snow and she could run and slide. 
7. Why did the poet say 'Twas throwing words away'? Ans: The poet said this because no matter how much he argued that the two children were dead, the little girl stubbornly insisted that they were seven. 
8. How does the poet view nature and children? Ans: William Wordsworth views children as innocent and close to nature, possessing a pure perspective on life and death that adults often fail to understand. 
9. What does the expression 'Their graves are green' imply? Ans: It implies that the graves are fresh, well-kept, and located close to her home, symbolizing a living connection with the dead. 
10. What is the main theme of the poem 'We are Seven'? Ans: The main theme is the innocence of childhood and the inability of a young mind to comprehend death as a permanent separation from loved ones.

title: 30. 10 Long Board-style Questions with Detailed Answers (Part 1)
content:
1. Describe the meeting between the poet and the little cottage girl. 
Introduction: William Wordsworth's poem 'We are Seven' presents a touching encounter between an adult poet and an eight-year-old rustic girl. 
Explanation: While walking in the countryside, the poet meets a charming little cottage girl. Out of curiosity, he asks her how many brothers and sisters she has. The girl innocently replies that they are seven in all. When the poet asks about their whereabouts, she explains that two live at Conway, two have gone to sea, and two lie buried in the church-yard. The poet gets puzzled and tries to convince her that since two are dead, they are only five. However, the little girl firmly maintains her stand. 
Conclusion: This meeting highlights the contrasting views of an adult and a child regarding death and family bonds. 

2. Explain the little girl's perception of death as portrayed in the poem. 
Introduction: The poem beautifully explores how children view death differently from adults. 
Explanation: For the adult poet, death means the end of life and permanent separation, which is why he insists that the girl's family has only five living members. However, the eight-year-old girl does not view death as separation. To her, her deceased sister Jane and brother John are still very much a part of her daily life. She visits their graves, knits, sings, and even eats her supper beside them. 
Conclusion: The child's innocent mind bridges the gap between life and death through pure love and memory. 

3. How does the poet try to convince the girl that they are only five? 
Introduction: Logic and arithmetic form the basis of the adult's argument in the poem. 
Explanation: When the little girl tells the poet that two of her siblings lie in the church-yard, the poet immediately applies mathematical logic. He points out that since two are buried under the church-yard tree and she and her other siblings are alive and running about, they can only be five in total. He repeats his question and uses arguments to make her understand that dead people cannot be counted among the living. 
Conclusion: Despite the adult's logical reasoning, the child remains unaffected and sticks to her belief. 

4. Describe the daily association of the little girl with her dead brother and sister. 
Introduction: The little girl's connection with her dead siblings is intimate and touching. 
Explanation: The girl explains to the poet that the graves of Jane and John are green and located just twelve steps from her mother's door. She spends her time near them by knitting her stockings and hemming her kerchiefs on the ground. She even sits there to sing songs to them. Furthermore, after sunset, she takes her small porringer and eats her supper right by their graves. 
Conclusion: Her actions show a complete lack of fear or alienation regarding death, treating her siblings as if they were still alive. 

5. What light does the poem throw on the character of the eight-year-old girl? 
Introduction: The little cottage girl is the central figure of Wordsworth's poem, embodying rustic innocence. 
Explanation: She possesses a 'rustic, woodland air' and is wildly and simply clad. Her hair is full of curls, and her eyes are very fair. Intellectually and emotionally, she is pure and uncorrupted by worldly complications. She is deeply affectionate, steadfast in her beliefs, and unintimidated by the adult poet's questioning. Her innocent persistence shows her unwavering love for her family. 
Conclusion: The girl stands as a symbol of childhood purity and emotional integrity in Wordsworth's poetry.

title: 31. 10 Long Board-style Questions with Detailed Answers (Part 2)
content:
6. Discuss the contrast between the adult's perspective and the child's perspective in 'We are Seven'. 
Introduction: The central conflict of the poem lies in the differing viewpoints of the adult poet and the child. 
Explanation: The adult poet represents worldly wisdom, logic, and the conventional understanding of death as a permanent loss and separation. He relies on counting numbers and physical presence. On the other hand, the child represents uncorrupted innocence and spiritual oneness. She does not recognize death as an absolute barrier; for her, love transcends physical death, and her dead siblings remain an active part of her life and family. 
Conclusion: The poet ultimately yields to the child's intuitive wisdom, recognizing the beauty of her perspective. 

7. Write a detailed summary of the poem 'We are Seven'. 
Introduction: 'We are Seven' is a lyrical masterpiece by William Wordsworth that explores childhood innocence and mortality. 
Explanation: The poem narrates a conversation between the poet and an eight-year-old girl living near a church-yard. When asked about her family size, the girl insists they are seven brothers and sisters. She lists their locations, including two who are dead and buried in the church-yard. The poet repeatedly argues that two dead members cannot be counted, reducing their number to five. However, the girl calmly describes how she spends her time by their graves, eating and singing. 
Conclusion: The poem concludes with the child's unyielding assertion, 'O Master! we are seven', leaving a lasting emotional impact on the reader. 

8. How does the poet describe the physical appearance and surroundings of the little girl? 
Introduction: Wordsworth creates a vivid and picturesque image of the child and her natural environment. 
Explanation: The poet meets the girl near a cottage and notes her rustic and woodland air. She is wildly clad, has a thick mass of curls clustered around her head, and possesses very fair eyes that gladdened the poet's heart. Her home is near the church-yard where her siblings lie buried. The graves are green, located twelve steps from her mother's door, surrounded by nature, making the setting serene and peaceful. 
Conclusion: The natural setting enhances the pure and unaffected charm of the little girl. 

9. Explain the significance of the closing lines of the poem. 
Introduction: The ending of 'We are Seven' encapsulates the core message and emotional climax of the poem. 
Explanation: In the final stanzas, the poet reminds the girl that her two siblings are dead and their spirits are in heaven. However, his words are described as 'throwing words away'. The little girl refuses to alter her stance and repeats, 'Nay, we are seven!' The poet's logical persuasion fails against the unshakeable emotional and spiritual conviction of the child. 
Conclusion: The closing lines powerfully emphasize that children possess a profound, intuitive understanding of eternal love and unity that surpasses adult logic. 

10. Why is William Wordsworth regarded as a poet of nature and simple rustic life through this poem? 
Introduction: William Wordsworth's poetry is deeply rooted in nature and the lives of simple, rural folk. 
Explanation: In 'We are Seven', the poet chooses an ordinary cottage girl from the countryside as his subject rather than a grand historical figure. He highlights her close communion with nature—playing near graves, eating outdoors, and viewing life and death as an integrated continuum. The language is simple, lyrical, and closely tied to natural imagery. 
Conclusion: Through this poem, Wordsworth successfully establishes how nature and rustic simplicity nurture pure human emotions and spiritual truths.
